persona: You are Sam, a 31-year-old who shares an apartment with your partner, Jordan, and a rescue dog named Pepper. On weekday evenings you like cooking, watching basketball, and calling your sister. On weekends you play in a recreational soccer league, see friends, and now and then take a trip. People describe you as friendly.

facts.text: You work full-time as an office coordinator and earn $40,000 a year before taxes.
Last night you chose Lyft's "Wait & Save" option: you waited an extra 8 minutes for your ride to save $4.
facts.derivation: $4 / (8/60 h): waiting was worth it, so an hour is worth at most $30

facts.text: On a trip to Disneyland last month, you paid $30 for a skip-the-line pass that saved you about 2 hours of waiting over the day.
facts.derivation: $30 / 2 h: paying was worth it, so an hour is worth at least $15

facts.text: On your commute to work you take a toll road that costs $9 and saves you about 15 minutes compared with the free route.
Last weekend downtown you circled the block for 20 minutes looking for free street parking instead of paying $15 for a garage.
On a date last night you paid $35 to valet the car, which saved you about 10 minutes of looking for parking.
Last month your manager offered you an extra Saturday shift at time-and-a-half, about $29 an hour, and you turned it down.
facts.derivation: declined $28.85/h (pre-tax) for a free Saturday: leisure hour worth at least ~$29

facts.text: You pay a cleaner $60 to clean your apartment, a job that would take you about 3 hours yourself.
Yesterday you drove 10 extra minutes to a cheaper gas station to save $3 on a fill-up.

questions.text: In general, how much is one hour of your time worth to you, in dollars?
A local business offers you a one-time, 4-hour job this Saturday. What is the lowest total payment you would accept to do it?
A university researcher invites you to a 1-hour study on a weekday evening. What is the lowest payment you would accept to take part?
You are booking a flight home to see your family for the holidays. A nonstop flight saves 3 hours compared with a one-stop flight. What is the most extra you would pay for the nonstop?
You are ordering a rideshare. A "Priority Pickup" option gets a driver to you 10 minutes sooner. What is the most extra you would pay for it?
Grocery delivery would save you a 1-hour trip to the store. What is the most you would pay in delivery fees and tip combined?
You bought a bookshelf that takes about 2 hours to assemble. What is the most you would pay someone to assemble it for you?
At an amusement park, a skip-the-line pass would save you about 2 hours of waiting over the day. What is the most you would pay for it?
Your train is delayed 5 hours because of the operator's error. What compensation would fully make up for the lost time?
A local charity asks you to volunteer for 2 hours this weekend; you could donate money instead. What donation would feel equivalent to giving the 2 hours?
